mainTopic: How many חטאות a person brings for doing many מלאכות on שבת by mistake, and which kind of forgetting (of שבת or of the מלאכות) decides the count
overview: This amud opens at the end of רבי יוסי's דרשה on the פסוק 'מאחת מהנה'. It teaches אבות and תולדות and two basic cases. In the first, a person knew it was שבת but forgot the מלאכות were forbidden, so he brings a חטאת for each מלאכה. In the second, he forgot it was שבת, so he brings one חטאת in total. The גמרא explains that שמואל does not learn those two cases from this פסוק. רבא then asks רב נחמן about a person who forgot both שבת and the מלאכות. רב אשי suggests a test based on what makes him stop working, but רבינא rejects it and concludes 'לא שנא': he counts as having forgotten שבת and brings one חטאת. The גמרא checks this against רבי יוחנן's reading of the משנה of 39 מלאכות. It shows that the 39 חטאות happen when he knew it was שבת but forgot the מלאכות, and this works even for ריש לקיש, through knowledge of תחומין according to רבי עקיבא. Finally רבא sets up a mixed case of reaping and grinding done twice, once with each kind of mistake, and discovered at two different times. His ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of רבי יוסי's derivation from 'מאחת מהנה'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי reads each word of 'מאחת מהנה' as a separate teaching: אבות, תולדות, forgetting the מלאכות, and forgetting שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Even a part of a word, like] 'שם' from 'שמעון'. 'הנה' (them) means the main labors (אבות). 'מהנה' (of them) means the sub-labors (תולדות). 'One that is them' means he knew it was שבת but did not know the labors were forbidden. 'Them that are one' means he forgot it was שבת but knew the labors were forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי יוסי, who finds four separate lessons hidden in the words of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'One that is them' describes one sin that becomes many חטאות: he knew it was שבת but forgot the מלאכות, so he brings a חטאת for each מלאכה. 'Them that are one' describes many acts that become one חטאת: he forgot it was שבת, so all his acts count as one mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: The main categories of forbidden labor
Sub-labors that come from the main categories
Not knowing that these labors are forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the reversal. In 'one that is them' he KNEW it was שבת and is liable for MANY. In 'them that are one' he FORGOT it was שבת and is liable for only ONE.
steps.whyThisMatters: These two cases are the basic framework for the whole discussion that follows about forgetting both things at once.

phrases.english: [like] 'Shem' from 'Shimon.'
phrases.notes: End of a sentence from the previous page: even a partial act counts, just as writing שם can be the start of שמעון.

phrases.english: 'Them' — the primary labors,
'Of them' — the subcategories.
'One that is them' —
aware of Shabbat but unaware that the labors are forbidden.
'Them that are one' —
unaware of Shabbat but aware that the labors are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוסי's דרשה, which began on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forgetting the מלאכות means a חטאת for each one; forgetting שבת means one חטאת in total.

steps.title: Why שמואל does not use this derivation
steps.stepSummary: שמואל does not read 'one that is them' and 'them that are one' into the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל? He does not understand 'one that is them' and 'them that are one' from this פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שמואל did not use רבי יוסי's source: he simply does not read those two lessons into the words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hidden question is: if רבי יוסי has a פסוק for dividing the מלאכות, why does שמואל need a different source? The answer is that שמואל does not accept this reading of the פסוק, so he must learn the law some other way.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not understand it that way

phrases.english: And Shmuel?
phrases.notes: An unspoken question: why doesn't he use this source?

phrases.english: 'one that is them' and 'them that are one'
he does not derive from the verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל, ״אַחַת שֶׁהִיא הֵנָּה״ וְ״הֵנָּה שֶׁהִיא אַחַת״ לָא מַשְׁמַע לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question of why שמואל disagrees with step 1.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל does not accept this דרשה.

steps.title: רבא asks about forgetting both at once
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן what the law is when a person forgot both that it is שבת and that the labors are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: if he forgot both this and that, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a new question: what happens when a person forgot both things at the same time?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 covered only cases where he forgot one thing and knew the other. Here both are forgotten, so it is unclear which rule wins: one חטאת in total, or one for each מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that (here: both שבת and the מלאכות)

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Naḥman:
if he forgot both this and that, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new mixed case from the two cases in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether forgetting both counts as forgetting שבת (one חטאת) or as forgetting the מלאכות (one for each).

steps.title: רב נחמן: he brings only one חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says that since he forgot שבת, he brings only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: he forgot שבת, so he is liable only once.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers that forgetting שבת is enough to make it all one mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן focuses on the forgetting of שבת. Once that is present, he applies the 'them that are one' rule from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: He is liable for only one (חטאת)

phrases.english: He said to him:
He had a lapse of awareness of Shabbat,
and is liable for only one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֲרֵי הֶעְלֵם שַׁבָּת בְּיָדוֹ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Forgetting שבת controls, so he brings one חטאת.

steps.title: רבא pushes back: he also forgot the מלאכות
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues the opposite: he also forgot the מלאכות, so he should bring a חטאת for each.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! He forgot the labors, so he should be liable for each and every one!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן with the opposite logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both kinds of forgetting are present, so why should forgetting שבת win? One could just as easily say that forgetting the מלאכות wins, which would mean many חטאות.

phrases.english: On the contrary, he had a lapse of awareness of the labors,
and should be liable for each and every one!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that forgetting שבת controls
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The opposite claim is equally strong, so רב נחמן's choice is arbitrary.

steps.title: רב אשי: see what makes him stop
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי suggests a test: whatever reminder makes him stop working shows which thing he had really forgotten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: we look. If he stops because of [being told it is] שבת, he had forgotten שבת and is liable only once. If he stops because of [being told about] the labor, he had forgotten the labors and is liable for each one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a practical test to decide between the two views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being told 'it's שבת' is what stops him, then forgetting שבת was the real cause, so he brings one חטאת. If being told 'this labor is forbidden' is what stops him, then forgetting the מלאכות was the real cause, so he brings many.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said: we see,
if he stops because of Shabbat —
then he had a lapse of awareness of Shabbat
and is liable for only one;
and if he stops because of the labor —
then he had a lapse of awareness of the labors
and is liable for each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a middle path between רב נחמן and רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Which thing he forgot is decided by what reminder makes him stop.

steps.title: רבינא: the test does not work, so there is no difference
steps.stepSummary: רבינא shows that the two reminders cannot be separated, so the test fails and he counts as having forgotten שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Does he stop because of שבת for any reason other than the labors? Does he stop because of the labors for any reason other than שבת? Rather, there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא knocks down רב אשי's test and concludes there is no difference between the cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being told 'it's שבת' stops him only because he now realizes the work is forbidden. Being told 'this work is forbidden' stops him only because he now realizes it is שבת. Each reminder works through the other, so the test proves nothing. The conclusion is that he counts as forgetting שבת and brings one חטאת.
steps.whatToRemember: When a person forgot both שבת and the מלאכות, the conclusion is 'לא שנא': he is treated as having forgotten שבת and brings only one חטאת.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוּם פֵּרֵישׁ מִשַּׁבָּת אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם מְלָאכוֹת,
phrases.english: Does he stop because of Shabbat for any reason but the labors?

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוּם פֵּרֵישׁ מִמְּלָאכוֹת אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם שַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: Does he stop from the labors for any reason but Shabbat?
Rather, there is no difference.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: כְּלוּם פֵּרֵישׁ מִשַּׁבָּת אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם מְלָאכוֹת
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole of רב אשי's test
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two reminders always depend on each other, so neither can be the single cause.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no difference; forgetting both is treated as forgetting שבת.

steps.title: Bringing in the משנה of 39 מלאכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה listing 39 אבות מלאכות and רבי יוחנן's explanation of why it gives a number.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: the main labors are forty minus one. We asked: why do I need the number? And רבי יוחנן said: if he did them all in one forgetting, he is liable for each one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a test of the previous conclusion by quoting a משנה and רבי יוחנן's explanation of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says the number 39 teaches the maximum number of חטאות a person can owe for one forgetting. This step is only background; the next step uses it to test the ruling of 'one חטאת'.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need the number?

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: אֲבוֹת מְלָאכוֹת אַרְבָּעִים חָסֵר אַחַת,
phrases.english: We learned: the primary labors are forty minus one,
and we discussed it: why do I need the tally?
And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
that if he did all of them in one lapse of awareness —
he is liable for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: אֲבוֹת מְלָאכוֹת אַרְבָּעִים חָסֵר אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings in a source to test the conclusion of step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doing all 39 in one forgetting means 39 חטאות.

steps.title: How can 39 חטאות happen if forgetting שבת means one?
steps.stepSummary: If forgetting both means only one חטאת, the גמרא asks what case רבי יוחנן's 39 חטאות could be describing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, if you say that forgetting both means he is liable for each one, that works. But if you say that forgetting שבת means only one, how can you find [the case of 39]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the conclusion of step 7 using רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simplest case of 'one forgetting' is a person who forgot everything. According to step 7, that person brings only one חטאת. So where does the 39 come from?

keyTerms.meaning: How can you find such a case?

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא הֶעְלֵם זֶה וָזֶה בְּיָדוֹ
phrases.english: Granted, if you say that if he forgot both this and that

phrases.aramaic: חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת — שַׁפִּיר,
phrases.english: he is liable for each one — fine;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ הֶעְלֵם שַׁבָּת בְּיָדוֹ
phrases.english: but if you say that since he forgot Shabbat
he is liable for only one,
how can you find it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא הֶעְלֵם זֶה וָזֶה בְּיָדוֹ
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that forgetting both means one חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's case of 39 seems impossible if forgetting שבת always reduces it to one.

steps.title: The case: he knew it was שבת but forgot the מלאכות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's case is a person who knew it was שבת but did not know the מלאכות were forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: With awareness of שבת and unawareness of the labors!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 39 חטאות happen when he knew it was שבת but forgot that these labors are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the 'one that is them' case from step 1. Because he did not forget שבת, each forgotten מלאכה brings its own חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: With knowledge that it is שבת

phrases.english: With awareness of Shabbat and unawareness of the labors!

steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן means a person who knew it was שבת but forgot the מלאכות.

steps.title: What did he know about שבת, according to ריש לקיש?
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי יוחנן's definition of שוגג the case works, but under ריש לקיש it is unclear what he knew about שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works if he holds like רבי יוחנן, who said that once he was unaware of כרת, even though he knew about the לאו [it counts as שוגג]. You find it where he knew that שבת has a לאו. But if he holds like ריש לקיש, who said [it is not שוגג] until he is unaware of both the לאו and כרת, then what did he know about שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 10: under ריש לקיש's view, what kind of 'knowing שבת' is left?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, he can know that working on שבת is a לאו and still be a שוגג because he does not know about כרת. For ריש לקיש, a שוגג must be unaware of both the לאו and כרת for every מלאכה. Then it seems he knows nothing at all about שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Being cut off, a punishment from Heaven

steps.confusionAlert: Here the name רבי יוחנן refers to a different dispute: the definition of שוגג (unaware of כרת alone, or of both the לאו and כרת). It is not about counting the 39 מלאכות.

phrases.aramaic: הָנִיחָא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: This works if he holds like Rabbi Yoḥanan,
who said: once he was unwitting about karet,
even though he was intentional about the prohibition,

phrases.aramaic: מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ דְּיָדַע לֵיהּ לְשַׁבָּת בְּלָאו.
phrases.english: you find it where he knew of Shabbat as a prohibition.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: But if he holds like Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,
who said: [not unwitting] until he is unwitting about both the prohibition and karet —
in what way did he know about Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case given in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of knowing שבת but forgetting the מלאכות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under ריש לקיש, being a שוגג on every מלאכה leaves no meaningful knowledge of שבת.

steps.title: He knew about תחומין, following רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: He knew the law of תחומין, which רבי עקיבא holds is a Torah law, so he did know something about שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He knew about it through תחומין, according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that his 'knowing שבת' was knowing the law of תחומין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, תחומין is a Torah law with a לאו. A person who knows about it knows that שבת exists as a day with Torah prohibitions, even while being fully a שוגג on all 39 מלאכות. So רבי יוחנן's case works under ריש לקיש too.

keyTerms.meaning: The limits on walking outside the town on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: Even under ריש לקיש, 'knowing it is שבת' can mean knowing about תחומין (a Torah law according to רבי עקיבא) while being a שוגג on all 39 מלאכות.

phrases.english: He knew about it through the Shabbat boundaries,
according to Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּיָדַע לֵהּ בִּתְחוּמִין, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.terutzMaskana: Knowing שבת means knowing about תחומין, which is a Torah law according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's case of 39 חטאות works even under ריש לקיש. So the challenge from step 9 is answered, and רבינא's ruling in step 7 stands: a person who forgot both שבת and the מלאכות brings only one חטאת.

steps.title: רבא describes a person who reaped and ground twice with two different kinds of mistakes
steps.stepSummary: רבא sets up a detailed case. A person did קצירה and טחינה once with שגגת שבת and זדון מלאכות, and again with זדון שבת and שגגת מלאכות. Then he found out about each set at a different time. The question about his חטאות comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Someone reaped and ground a dried-fig amount while he forgot it was שבת but knew these מלאכות were forbidden. Then he reaped and ground a dried-fig amount again, this time knowing it was שבת but not knowing these מלאכות were forbidden. Later he found out about the reaping and grinding he did when he forgot שבת. After that he found out about the reaping and grinding he did when he forgot the מלאכות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is building a case step by step to prepare a question. This step only lays out the facts. The ruling or question comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps taught that forgetting it is שבת (שגגת שבת) brings only one חטאת for many מלאכות. Forgetting that the מלאכות are forbidden (שגגת מלאכות) brings a separate חטאת for each מלאכה. רבא mixes both kinds of mistake with the same two מלאכות and has the person find out at two different times. That sets up the question of whether the first discovery and its חטאת also cover the second set.

keyTerms.meaning: Forgot it was שבת, but knew the מלאכות are forbidden. This brings one חטאת for everything done in that lapse.
Knew it was שבת, but did not know the מלאכות are forbidden. This brings one חטאת for each separate מלאכה.
The size of a dried fig. This is the minimum amount of food that makes one liable for reaping or grinding.
Reaping, one of the 39 אבות מלאכות.
Grinding, one of the 39 אבות מלאכות.
He became aware that he sinned. Becoming aware is what obligates a person to bring a חטאת.

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two sets apart. The first set is forgetting שבת, which means one חטאת total. The second set is forgetting the מלאכות, which means one חטאת per מלאכה. Both sets involve the same two מלאכות (reaping and grinding). That overlap is exactly what רבא is going to ask about.
steps.whyThisMatters: This case tests how a discovery and a חטאת for one kind of mistake connect to the same מלאכות done under a different kind of mistake. It pushes the earlier rules about שגגת שבת versus שגגת מלאכות into a harder, mixed situation.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Someone reaped and ground a dried-fig amount
phrases.notes: A dried-fig amount is the minimum measure for liability.

phrases.english: while unaware it was Shabbat but aware the labors were forbidden,
and then he again reaped and ground a dried-fig amount
phrases.notes: He had not yet realized his first sin.

phrases.english: while aware it was Shabbat but unaware the labors were forbidden,
and he became aware of the reaping and grinding
done while unaware of Shabbat and aware of the labors,
phrases.notes: This discovery is about the first set only.

phrases.aramaic: וְחָזַר וְנוֹדַע לוֹ עַל קְצִירָה וְעַל טְחִינָה
phrases.english: and then he became aware of the reaping and the grinding
done while aware of Shabbat and unaware of the labors —
phrases.notes: The dash shows that רבא's question or ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: קָצַר וְטָחַן כִּגְרוֹגֶרֶת בְּשִׁגְגַת שַׁבָּת וּזְדוֹן מְלָאכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of רבי יוחנן's 39 חטאות and the definitions of שוגג, רבא opens a new case. It combines the two categories from step 1, שגגת שבת and שגגת מלאכות, involving the same מלאכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This is the factual setup of a mixed case: two sets of reaping and grinding, each done with a different kind of mistake and discovered at a different time. It prepares a question about how the חטאות relate.
